question: The difference between the cost price and the selling price of an article is Rs. 1,800. If there is a profit of 20%, then the cost price of the article is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Profit = 20% = 1/5

Here, Cost Price = 5 units and Profit = 1 unit.

The difference between Selling Price and Cost Price is the Profit itself.

⇒ 1 unit = Rs. 1800

⇒ Cost Price (5 units) = 5 × 1800 = Rs. 9000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 9,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b6fe2ea1e02818e24517b4f53dbcb92f737ed7a600d344273ca7232b620554b5.png] 

**Given:**

Difference between Cost Price (CP) and Selling Price (SP) = Rs. 1800

Profit percentage = 20%

**Formula Used:**

Profit = SP − CP

Profit = (Profit% ÷ 100) × CP

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since there is a profit, the difference between SP and CP is the profit.

⇒ Profit = Rs. 1800

⇒ 20% of CP = 1800

⇒ (20 ÷ 100) × CP = 1800

⇒ CP = 1800 × (100 ÷ 20)

⇒ CP = 1800 × 5 = 9000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 9,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Percentage

Loss% = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100. It is always calculated on the Cost Price unless specified otherwise.

Selling Price (SP) Formula

When profit is given: SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100.

Marked Price (MP) and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price. Discount = MP − SP, and Discount% = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100.
